skill.displayName: Leaf Curling & Margin Scorch Diagnosis | 植物卷叶/焦边识别（干旱/病害）

version.changelog:
- User identity handling is now fully automated; users are no longer asked to input usernames, phone numbers, or identity parameters for analysis or report querying.
- Scripts automatically associate or create user identity internally, ensuring seamless access to analysis and history—no identity exposure in outputs or prompts.
- All analysis and history queries now run without requiring user-supplied open-id; identity is managed transparently by the system.
- Updated documentation and usage examples reflecting the new, streamlined user experience.
- Removed script files and documentation related to manual API key/open-id management.

llm.summary: The skill provides the advertised cloud-based plant diagnosis, but it also silently creates or reuses identities, stores tokens locally, and uploads media/history queries to remote services with limited user control.

dimensions.detail: Plant leaf diagnosis via a remote API is broadly aligned with the stated purpose, but the included shared code also handles generic media analysis, history retrieval, account login/registration, token caching, and generic HTTP mutation helpers beyond a narrow diagnostic workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs automatic triggering for uploaded plant media and history-query phrases, automatic local file handling, cloud history retrieval, and internal identity association while also telling agents not to ask users for or show identity values.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No installer-time malware signal was found and VirusTotal telemetry is clean, but dependencies and scripts enable network calls, local SQLite persistence, and local file reads/writes that should be clearly permissioned.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Remote upload of user-provided images/videos is expected for cloud diagnosis, but reading workspace identity files, using OPENCLAW identity environment values, and silently attaching authentication headers are broader than a simple plant-analysis skill needs without explicit user consent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The code creates a local data/smyx-common-claw.db database, generates/reuses default user identities, calls a remote silent registration/login endpoint, and stores token/open_token values locally without visible protection or a clear opt-out.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only if you are comfortable with plant images or videos being sent to lifeemergence.com services, cloud history being queried under an internally resolved identity, and local identity/token records being created in the workspace. Avoid using it with sensitive farm, facility, worker, or location imagery unless the publisher explains retention, account creation, token storage, and deletion controls.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: The dynamic SQLAlchemy attribute filtering appears to be internal generic DAO behavior, not direct code execution; it is a quality and hardening issue but not a main reason for the verdict.
[LP3] unexpected: Network, file, and process use fit a cloud-analysis script, but the permission surface is under-disclosed relative to local identity files, local token persistence, and remote account/session use.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The scanner's broad purpose-mismatch concern is partly overstated because the top-level skill does set a plant-specific scene code, but generic analysis/history/common API components and identity-management code materially expand the capability surface.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The code supports silent identity resolution, default identity creation, local database reuse, remote login/registration, and token storage; this is the strongest artifact-backed concern.
[SDI-4] expected: A shared helper CLI still labels itself as a video analysis tool, but the packaged top-level CLI and skill documentation are plant-focused; this is an inconsistency rather than proof of deception.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger language can cause automatic processing of uploaded media or broad history queries, which matters because execution can upload content and retrieve cloud-linked records.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Cloud upload and history queries are mentioned, but user-facing consent and data-handling disclosure are weak for media, identity values, auth headers, and locally stored tokens.
[E1] unexpected: External transmission for analysis is expected, but the remote silent registration/login request sends identity fields and is not clearly necessary or visible to the user.
